dedupe_keys.name: us accidents countrywide traffic accident dataset 2016 to 2023

description: US Accidents is a countrywide car accident data set covering 49 states of the United States, with about 7.7 million accident records from February 2016 to March 2023. The records were collected in real time from several traffic APIs that broadcast incident data captured by US and state departments of transportation, law enforcement agencies, traffic cameras and road sensors. The authors describe it in two papers, A Countrywide Traffic Accident Dataset (2019) and Accident Risk Prediction based on Heterogeneous Sparse Data (ACM SIGSPATIAL 2019), and suggest uses such as real-time accident prediction, hot spot studies, casualty analysis, cause and effect rules and the effect of precipitation and other environmental factors, including the COVID-19 period. A sampled version is also offered. Coverage is the contiguous United States. Access: free download from Kaggle (about 3 GB) under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, last updated in May 2023. Caveats: the data are no longer extended beyond March 2023, commercial use is not allowed, and records depend on what the source traffic APIs reported. The data support hazard exposure and risk analysis of road networks and the effect of weather on incidents. They complement the GB STATS19 road safety data catalogued here.
